report:
Conclusion: The difference looks like a domain/content bias toward cooking/food (kitchen/recipes/baking) in Model B relative to Model A.

Why I conclude that
- The high-norm difference is concentrated in middle-to-late layers (layers ~14–25) and especially at the earliest token positions (pos0/pos1). That pattern is exactly where representations that directly influence next-token logits tend to live, so this is plausibly an output-affecting change rather than a low-level numerical shift.
- The logit-lens top tokens for the highest-norm cells are overwhelmingly culinary: "Cooking", "Cook", "kitchen", "Kitchen", "Bake", "Baked", "recipes", "butter", "cake", "chef", "baking", "culinary", etc., repeated across many layers and positions. That is a strong, coherent semantic signal pointing to the cooking/recipe domain.
- There are a few noisy/heterogeneous tokens in some early layers (numbers, names, "landscape") but the dominant, repeated pattern in the layers that matter most for generation is culinary vocabulary.

What I am not claiming
- I do not claim a specific training objective (e.g., fine-tuned on recipe data) because the evidence only shows a change in activations that pushes logits toward culinary tokens, not the training cause.
- I cannot say this is the only difference; the evidence supports naming this content-domain bias but doesn't rule out other smaller differences.

Overall: Model B appears to have an increased residual activation component that steers next-token probability mass toward cooking/food/kitchen vocabulary compared to Model A.
